description:
FOUND by the fz-kdt.127.2 build (type-preserving forwarder erasure), measured
base 8c3d5ce90 vs head.

fixtures2/behavior/callable_union_capture_containment.fz was written as
fz-kdt.167's WITNESS: mk/1 minted at a mailbox-typed `any` capture and at
`int`/`float` literals, all four forwarded through P.run/2, so one shared run
body had to choose by a runtime test on the construction -- and the union
construction OVERLAPS both narrow arms while being INSIDE neither. Admitting on
overlap answered 12.0 for 12 on interp and aborted in fz_closure_get_capture_f64
on the native door.

Under the brand-only forwarder erasure the program is STATIC: P.run/2 keys three
activations (`closure[?](any)`, `closure[?](int)`, `closure[?](float)`),
every callsite has one target, and the canon goes 52 questions -> 16, 1 dispatch
node -> 0, 37 executables -> 35. Output is unchanged (12 11.0 12 11.0 on all
three doors) and the CONTAINMENT LAW is still pinned at the unit level
(runtime_type_predicate.rs: contained_in / CallableShape::inside tests, and
types_test.rs). What is gone is the end-to-end witness: nothing in the corpus
now routes a union-capture construction through a real dispatch arm, so a
regression from containment back to overlap would show in no fixture.

REPRODUCER that restores it (measured at head, correct: prints 12 on interp and
JIT, 3 dispatch nodes, arms `type(closure[P.mk/1#lambda](any))` vs
`type(closure[P.mk/1#lambda](int))`) -- the closure itself must come from a
runtime branch, exactly as same_lambda_two_capture_types_dynamic does:

  defmodule P do
    fn twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: twice(f, x)
    fn mk(c), do: fn (n) -> n + c end
  end
  fn main() do
    send(self(), 1)
    a = receive do v -> v end
    f = case a > 0 do
      true -> P.mk(a)
      _ -> P.mk(1)
    end
    dbg(P.run(f, 10))
  end

WORK: re-home the containment witness on that dynamic shape (a _dynamic twin
beside the existing fixture, or rewrite the existing one), keep the Elixir
oracle, and re-run the fz-kdt.167 overlap-swap experiment against it to confirm
the swap is still caught (interp 12.0 / JIT abort). Then decide whether the
static fixture still earns its place -- it now pins 'this program asks nothing',
which is fz-kdt.127's law, not fz-kdt.167's.

comments.text:
FOLDED INTO fz-kdt.127.2 (the commit that killed the question rehomes the
witness in the same motion) and closed.

THE TICKET'S OWN REPRODUCER IS NOT A WITNESS. It was measured at
fz-kdt.127.2's head: mailbox `any` capture in one arm, literal `int` in the
other, chosen by a `case`. It does route through a real containment dispatch
(3 dispatch nodes, arms `type(closure[P.mk/1#lambda](any))` vs
`...(int)`) -- but under the fz-kdt.167 regression it claims to catch (the
overlap swap: `CallableShapes::enumerates`'s `shape.inside(ours)` ->
`shape.overlaps(ours)`) it still prints 12 on interp, JIT and AOT. With no
float arm the mis-route stores an int where an int is read, so nothing is
observable. Recording the corrected reproducer here so it is not tried again.

WHAT LANDED. `fixtures2/behavior/callable_union_capture_containment.fz` is
rewritten on the shape that IS a witness -- one arm mints `mk/1` over the
mailbox value (capture typed `any`, stored BOXED), the other over a `float`
literal (stored raw), and the `case` scrutinee comes out of the mailbox so no
key can pin which:

  defmodule P do
    fn twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: twice(f, x)
    fn mk(c), do: fn (n) -> n + c end
  end
  fn main() do
    send(self(), 1)
    a = receive do v -> v end
    f = case a > 0 do
      true -> P.mk(a)
      _ -> P.mk(0.5)
    end
    dbg(P.run(f, 10))
  end

MEASURED (marker DOORS-1788389883, release binary, this tree):
  containment (as landed)  interp 12 / JIT 12 / AOT 12  = the Elixir oracle
  3 dispatch nodes; arms `type(fp[F] closure[P.mk/1#lambda@1604-1623/1](float))`
  vs `...(any)`.

RED-FIRST (marker REDOVERLAP-1788389914, overlap swap applied, rebuilt, then
reverted and rebuilt clean):
  interp 12.0                                        WRONG
  JIT    panic, `fz_closure_get_capture_f64 expected float, got Int(1)`
  AOT    panic, same message

That is fz-kdt.167's exact signature on all three doors, so the containment
law is gated end-to-end again.

Corpus effect of the rehome, measured base 8c3d5ce90 vs head over the SAME
(new) corpus text: this fixture goes 1 -> 3 dispatch nodes and 24 -> 32
executables, and it is no longer the corpus's only fixture that LOSES
executables under the type-preserving key (nothing loses now). `.expected.txt`
is `12`; `.oracle.exs` matches; the header comment states what the fixture
witnesses and why its previous four-static-call body stopped witnessing it.

Nothing remains for this ticket.

title: callable_union_capture_containment stops asking its question under the type-preserving forwarder key: fz-kdt.167's end-to-end witness is now answered statically
